what_it_does: Chip-to-chip communication over short distances (a few inches) at very high speed requires both signal conditioning and precise clock recovery. This paper presents a receiver that doubles the bandwidth while quadrupling the sampling rate—all while staying within strict power and area budgets. The key innovation is slicing: instead of trying to do all the filtering in one stage, the receiver breaks it into multiple stages, each handling part of the problem. A smart clock generator using phase interpolation creates eight different clock phases to precisely sample incoming data, enabling the high-speed communication at 224 gigabits per second while consuming just 1.11 picojoules per bit.
